title: chat.v1 output adaptor: prioritized stop signals and streaming logprob fallback for OpenAI /v1 parity
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: customers expect /v1/chat.completions parity for structured output, sensible stop semantics, and graceful streaming when upstream models omit logprobs. This PR introduces a focused compatibility adaptor that sits in the chatv1 parameter layer and the streaming coordinator to: 1) coalesce role metadata into a stable structured-output envelope (preserve role aliases and attach source metadata) so downstream tooling and analytics can rely on deterministic keys; 2) implement a prioritized stop arbitration layer that accepts multiple stop sources (explicit `stop` param, system-enforced sentinels, and runtime heuristic sentinels) and emits a deterministic stop reason with configurable priority and soft/hard semantics; 3) add a streaming logprob fallback that synthesizes conservative token-probability estimates when the backend returns no logprobs (avoids breaking token-level scorers and rerankers in streaming mode); 4) wire a short-lived streaming handshake for function/toolcall events to avoid interleaving partial tool payloads across fragments; 5) include a compatibility shim for OpenAI-style role arrays (user/assistant/system) so legacy clients see exact shape while we keep internal canonical structure. What changed: chatv1 adaptor and param normalization that maps /v1 semantics to internal runtime flags, a stop-priority arbiter implemented in streaming/stream_coordinator, a small logprob estimator module with conservative heuristics and tests, update to function-call streaming framing to include handshake markers, and docs + examples showing expected framed JSON. Testing: unit tests cover the arbiter matrix and fallback modes, integration test simulates an upstream model that omits logprobs and verifies downstream scorers remain functional. Backwards/forwards compatibility: feature is guarded behind a flag `compat.v1_chat_output_adaptor` (default on for hosted) and the logprob fallback is configurable per-tenant. Migration notes: none required for stored prompts; consumers relying on raw token-level logprobs should enable the experimental flag and validate. See linked Linear items for rollout plan and canary criteria.

review_comments: Luis Ortega: The arbiter matrix looks good but we need explicit coverage for overlapping stop tokens and streaming prefix truncation - please add a test for stop that crosses fragment boundary.
Maya Chen: Added cross-fragment stop test in integration suite and documented the expected behavior in the streaming doc. PTAL.
Zara Patel: Can we make the logprob fallback conservative by default? Concerned about downstream rerankers getting optimistic scores.

Maya Chen: Fallback returns -Inf probabilities as a sentinel for unknown when configured `mode=conservative`. Default heuristic returns a low-prob lookup (-12 to -6 logp) but migration flag can force conservative behavior.
Evan Kim: Lint failures on initial push (import order) — resolved in second commit.
Zara Patel: Approved pending small doc nit (remove duplicate example snippet).
ci_checks: integration-tests: pass (flaky upstream simulated run retried)
release_notes: Added OpenAI /v1 chat compatibility adaptor that provides structured output envelopes, prioritized stop arbitration, streaming logprob fallback, and a function-call handshake to improve parity and streaming stability.
notes_for_ops: Rollout plan: enable feature flag in staging for 48h with telemetry on stop_reason distribution and logprob_fallback.rate. Canary criteria: no increase in chat request errors >1% and no degradation in median streaming latency >15%.
example_request_response: Request: POST /v1/chat/completions with roles array + stop param. Response (streamed): framed JSON envelope events including role metadata, delta tokens, potential tool-call handshake events, and final `stop_reason` with priority tag. See docs file modified in this PR for exact shapes.
qa_instructions: Run unit tests: pytest redwood/tests/unit/test_stop_arbiter.py; integration: pytest redwood/tests/integration/test_streaming_logprob_fallback.py --simulate-no-logprobs; manual: run example toolcall_handshake.ts and confirm tool payloads are not interleaved across fragments.

notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: feature defaults to on for hosted API customers while enterprise/private deployments may opt into the behaviour via `compat.v1_chat_output_adaptor`. We monitored token-level telemetry in staging for 72 hours before merge.
